title: Elections, races and candidates
description: The #elections section: three race blocks holding fourteen candidates at the time of the audit. Candidates are a FLAT top-level array joined to races by race_id, not nested inside races, so a person who is both a sitting official and a candidate (Kristen Burke) is described once.

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema file.

election_date.description: Election day (YYYY-MM-DD). ONE value for the whole file -- the audit found this date written out in four places. Every rendering derives from here.

polling_hours.description: e.g. '6am - 9pm'. Shown in the voter info row.

editorial_note.description: The gold non-endorsement box above the races. Safe HTML subset.

voter_info.description: The three boxes below the races (Election Date / Register to Vote / Where to Vote). PAGE-LEVEL, not per-race: there is one row serving all three races, and nesting it under each race would create three copies of one fact.

value.description: The large figure or phrase, e.g. '6am - 9pm'. May contain {{fact:<id>}} tokens.

note.description: Small print under the value. Safe HTML subset -- these carry links and phone numbers.

debates.description: The Candidate Debates block at the top of the elections page, the debate line in the home banner, and the debates paragraph of the AI prompt. Dates, times and places are NOT written here: each event points at a facts.json entry whose display carries them, so the page, the banner and the prompt cannot disagree.

organizer_url.description: The organizer's site, where any remote-meeting link will be posted.

questions_url.description: Where residents submit questions for the debates.

hide_after.description: YYYY-MM-DD, the last debate. app.js removes the block and the banner line after this day, so they need no rebuild to retire.

race_id.description: A races[].id; the card links to that race's panel.

title.description: e.g. 'Town Clerk'. Also used in the pre-filled Ask Pelham question.

fact_ref.description: facts.json id. Its display is the when-and-where line, its value (YYYY-MM-DD) the date used in the Ask Pelham question, and its qualifier the matchup.

candidates.description: All candidates across all races. Rendered grouped by race_id then party_style, in array order within each group.

profile_methodology.description: Rendered once, above the races: how to read a thin profile. Separate from editorial_note, which is the non-endorsement statement.

id.description: Stable slug, the join target for candidate.race_id.

body.description: Foreign key to bodies.json id. Supplies the governing body name printed on the race header.

title.description: Office(s) contested, e.g. 'Board of Trustees' or 'Town Supervisor & Town Clerk'. A race block may cover two offices -- see candidate.office.

seats.description: Number of seats up. Drives the 'top N vote-getters win' line.

term_length.description: e.g. '2-year terms'. Printed in the race meta line.

badge.description: The pill on the right of the race header: 'First contested race since 2019', 'Re-run required by new state law'.

note.description: Optional explanatory box above the candidate grid. Only the Town race uses one today, for the state-law change forcing a re-run. Safe HTML subset.

context.description: The 'Context:' paragraph below the grid -- retirements, prior margins, how the seats are decided. Safe HTML subset plus {{fact:<id>}} tokens.

show_seats.description: Whether to print the seat count in the race meta line. False for a race block covering two different offices (Town Supervisor and Town Clerk), where a combined seat count is meaningless and the page has never shown one.

debate_summary.description: Optional. Manually written, AI-assisted summaries of a debate in this race, organized by topic. Each is shown under its own debate card in the Candidate Debates block, collapsed behind 'View debate summary', and given to the AI prompt. Matched to a debates.events entry by race and date, and by title as well when this race holds two debates that day (Town Clerk and Town Supervisor share a race); the build fails if a summary matches no debate. The page adds the AI-generated disclaimer and the recording link itself, so they cannot be left off. Omit or leave null until a debate has been transcribed.

title.description: Which debate, e.g. 'Village of Pelham Manor Board of Trustees'. Used in the recording link, and to tell apart two debates in one race on the same day (it must then equal the debates.events title).

recording_url.description: The full debate recording, linked from the disclaimer.

topics.description: DISPLAY ORDER IS ARRAY ORDER. Group what candidates said by subject. List a candidate under a topic only if they spoke to it, and keep related points from both sides under the same topic.

positions.description: One entry per candidate who spoke to this topic. Each candidate_id must be in this race; the build fails otherwise.

point.description: One sentence attributed in the candidate's voice, starting with a neutral verb ('Says', 'Argued', 'Noted', 'Proposed'). Never stated as fact, and no loaded verbs ('claimed', 'insisted', 'correctly noted'). Safe HTML subset; {{fact:}} tokens allowed.

id.description: Stable slug. Where the candidate is also a sitting official, use the same slug as their officials.json entry.

race_id.description: Foreign key to a races[].id. Build fails on a dangling reference.

office.description: Which seat this person seeks, e.g. 'Town Supervisor' or 'Town Clerk'. REQUIRED in practice for the Town race, whose single block contains two different offices; null where the race has only one.

party.description: Party line as DISPLAYED, e.g. 'Neighborhood Party . Republican' or 'Neighborhood Party'. Free text: the same styling is used for both of those labels.

party_style.description: Column colour only; renders as CSS class .party-label.<value>. Separate from party for the same reason issue tags split label from style.

incumbent.description: Whether they currently hold the seat. Lets the build render a consistent badge instead of relying on the meta line saying so.

meta.description: The one-line credential strip under the name: 'Incumbent . First elected 2020 . Running for third term'.

no_statement_as_of.description: Optional ISO date. Set when the candidate has published no campaign statement as of that date: the empty 'Why they say they're running' slot then reads 'No campaign statement has been published as of <date>.' in the muted not-found style, so a thin profile reads as a checked gap rather than an oversight. The build fails if this is set while why_running has content -- remove it once a statement is published.

source_url.description: Link to the reporting this profile is drawn from.

profile.description: The six-slot profile every candidate is rendered through, in a fixed order, so no candidate gets a longer or more favourable shape than another. A slot the public record does not fill is null and renders as an explicit "not found" line rather than being silently dropped -- an absent slot must read as a gap in the record, not as a judgement about the campaign. The sixth slot, Source, is source_url plus source_label.

background.description: Who they are and what they do. Safe HTML subset plus {{fact:<id>}} tokens.

why_running.description: Their stated reason for running, always attributed to them ("he says", "she argues") so the site never adopts a candidate rationale as its own voice. Null where no statement of intent exists in the public record.

prior_service.description: Elected or appointed public service. The literal string "No prior elected office." where there is none -- never null, because an empty slot here would read as missing research rather than as a fact about the candidate.

priorities.description: Stated campaign priorities, one per item. Where several candidates signed one joint platform they each carry its pledges, which is accurate: they each signed it.

quotes.description: Direct quotes from the public record, verbatim. Null where the record carries none.
